parsed.summary: The file proves four facts about R_k(3), defined as the least n such that every k-colouring of E(K_n) has a monochromatic triangle. (1) R_k^{1/k} → ∞. (2) For all k ≥ 2, R_k ≥ ((1/(6e^{38})) k^{1/3}/log k)^k, together with (1) again. (3) For every ε > 0, eventually (1/3−ε) k log k ≤ log R_k ≤ (1+ε) k log k. (4) log R_k = Θ(k log k). These match Theorem 1.1, its corollaries and eq. (4), with an explicit constant in place of the existential c; the only caveat is the sInf-based definition, which is sound for k ≥ 1 and gives an irrelevant junk-like value R_0 = 2.

glossary.plain: A k-colouring C of the edges of K_n (on Fin n) such that no colour class contains a triangle (3-clique).
Every k-colouring of E(K_n) has some colour class containing a triangle.
glossary.note: For k = 0 and n ≥ 2 there are no colourings, so the property holds vacuously.

glossary.plain: R_k(3) = min{n : every k-colouring of K_n has a monochromatic triangle}, taken as sInf in ℕ.
glossary.note: The set is nonempty for k ≥ 1 by Ramsey's theorem, so the value is genuine. For k = 0 the value is 2, which is a convention issue irrelevant to the asymptotics.

lean_claims.plain: For every integer k ≥ 2, ((1/(6e^{38})) · k^{1/3} / log k)^k ≤ R_k(3); and R_k(3)^{1/k} → ∞.
For every ε > 0, for all sufficiently large k: (1/3 − ε) k log k ≤ log R_k(3) ≤ (1 + ε) k log k.
log R_k(3) = Θ(k log k) as k → ∞.

paper_claims.plain: There exists an absolute constant c > 0 such that R_k(3) ≥ (c k^{1/3}/log k)^k for every integer k ≥ 2.
The Shannon capacity of graphs with independence number 2 is unbounded.

coverage.why: An explicit constant c = 1/(6e^{38}) is given instead of an existential one.
The ε-eventually form is exactly the meaning of the o(1) exponents.
R_k = k^{Θ(k)} is equivalent to log R_k = Θ(k log k).
No Shannon capacity statement appears in the file.

flags.explanation: For k = 0 there are no colourings of K_n with n ≥ 2, so the vacuous truth gives R_0 = 2. This is a convention point only and does not affect any asymptotic or k ≥ 2 statement.
Using an explicit constant 1/(6e^{38}) is stronger than the paper's existential c; this is acceptable.
The Shannon capacity reformulation is not formalized.
